_read_me: THE DEFAULT IS OFF. autonomous_operation_enabled is false, so a merged
orchestrator does not start spending money because a workflow fired. The
owner turns it on deliberately, in one place, and can turn it off the same
way. Every limit below starts conservative on purpose: a limit that was
never reached costs nothing, and a limit discovered by a bill is the
expensive way to learn where it should have been.
This file is in PROTECTED_PATHS. No worker may edit it; the orchestrator
reads it and refuses if it is missing or malformed.

CONTINUATION, not push recursion. GitHub does not start a workflow from a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN, so the loop advances by an explicit repository_dispatch instead. max_continuations_per_hour is the bound on that chain; max_runs_per_hour bounds every pass however it started.

MODE AUTHORITY IS PROTECTED STATE, NOT AN EVENT PAYLOAD. An earlier dispatcher let a human pick LIVE at startup and then downgraded every continuation to MOCK, because trusting the payload would have let anyone who can open a dispatch spend money. That was the right refusal and the wrong place to make the decision: it also meant LIVE could not survive its own first continuation. execution_mode moves the decision here, where it is committed, reviewable, and out of a worker's reach.
enabled_note: Set true to arm the loop. See coordination/AUTONOMY_SETUP.md. The kill switch is setting this back to false and pushing, which takes effect on the next orchestration pass.
execution_mode_note: MOCK | LIVE. THE ONLY SOURCE OF AUTHORITY FOR SPENDING MONEY. LIVE requires BOTH autonomous_operation_enabled=true AND execution_mode=LIVE, in this file, on the automation branch. A repository_dispatch payload can never grant it: the dispatcher reads this file after checkout and derives the mode from it, and the orchestrator re-checks in-process before any provider call. Either field is a kill switch on its own -- false stops the pass before a worker is reached, MOCK lets the pass run against fixtures with no paid call.

limit_notes.max_transitions_per_invocation: One orchestration pass may move the state machine at most this many times, then stops with TRANSITION_BUDGET_SPENT and lets the next GitHub event continue. This is what stops a runaway loop inside a single workflow run.
limit_notes.max_retries_per_task: A task that has already failed once gets one more attempt. A GOVERNANCE refusal is never retried at all, at any count -- see contracts.NEVER_AUTO_RETRY.
limit_notes.max_runs_per_hour: Counted from HANDOFF_LOG.jsonl, not from a wall clock the workflow controls, so two racing runners see the same number.
limit_notes.max_continuations_per_hour: A pass that finishes with work still eligible asks GitHub for one more pass via repository_dispatch. This caps how many such requests may be made in an hour, counted from HANDOFF_LOG.jsonl rather than from the payload -- the payload carries a chain depth for tracing, but a number the sender chose is not a number the receiver should enforce on.

branch_policy.require_task_branch_note: Start on the existing working branch so the first autonomous runs are visible in one place. Flip to true to make every task its own branch; dispatch.py already emits the branch name it would use.

dry_run_note: MOCK_PROVIDER is the default when AUTONOMY_MODE is unset, so the expensive mode has to be asked for by name rather than arrived at by forgetting a variable.
